clue.text: Head examiner slammed poor English teaching primarily

indicators.note: to be slammed is to be knocked about, so the letters of the two words before it are battered into a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word teaching is wanted

explanation.surface: An inspector criticises a school for its weak English lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slammed' shuffles POOR ENGLISH; 'primarily' adds the T of teaching at the end. 'Head examiner' looks like a chief inspector but is someone who studies skulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrenologist claimed to read character from the bumps of the skull, literally examining heads.

clue.text: Lowering sound, crooner admits hint of laryngitis

parts.note: a hum is a low sound

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the crooner's name takes in a letter

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, here the first letter of laryngitis

explanation.surface: A singer with a sore throat finds a croaky note humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbling someone brings them down in status or pride, reducing their standing.

clue.text: Old flame with sort of appeal is way out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
it means sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: Leaving an ex-partner who still has charm is the escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or route by which one leaves.

clue.text: Trouble with day working? Sticking at it, no matter what

definitions.text: Sticking at it, no matter what

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked over, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough day at work, and someone keeps going regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting stubbornly and refusing to yield is the sense of persisting whatever happens.

clue.text: Old sailors had to be decorated

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
to have a meal is to eat, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: Veteran sailors were obliged to be honoured with medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately embellished, heavily adorned.

clue.text: One crazy person on French island no good for anything

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nut is a madman
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A madman stranded on a French island is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inutile is a rare word for useless, serving no purpose.

clue.text: Use the rat-run possibly, making journey with a purpose

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged otherwise, a rearrangement of the phrase

explanation.surface: Taking a back-street shortcut to get somewhere with intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles USE THE RAT-RUN; a rat-run is a minor road drivers use to dodge main traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure hunt is a game in which players travel following clues towards a prize.

clue.text: Italian workers united — bad goings-on half concealed

parts.note: TU is a trade union, workers joined together

indicators.note: with half concealed only the front part of the word for misconduct stays visible

parts.note: a scandal is disgraceful behaviour

explanation.surface: An Italian union hushes up some wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan describes Tuscany, a region of Italy, or its people.

clue.text: Island school with university entrance

indicators.note: an entrance is a way in, so the university abbreviation goes into the word for school

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: An island's school has a link to a university admissions route.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM, a school of whales, is a crossword favourite; 'school' is not a place of learning here.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a Pacific island, a US territory in the Marianas.

clue.text: Agreement at home — something taken out overnight?

parts.note: someone at home is in
false teeth, a denture, are removed before bed

explanation.surface: A deal is struck at home, with a puzzle about what gets removed at night.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, such as one binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Focused study needing minimal money deemed very good

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
a cent is a tiny coin
rated means highly regarded

explanation.surface: Intense revision on a shoestring budget is judged excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated attention is attention directed at one thing, intent.

clue.text: Mysterious firm backed religious group

indicators.note: backed suggests going backwards, so the abbreviation for firm is reversed

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a cult is a small religious sect

explanation.surface: A shadowy company has given money to a sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult things are hidden and secret, beyond ordinary understanding, so mysterious.

clue.text: In favour of youngsters reportedly getting dietary requirements

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: reportedly says what follows is heard rather than seen, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: teens are teenagers, youngsters

explanation.surface: Supporters of teenagers want them to get proper nutrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns TEENS into the sound-alike TEINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins are nutrients the body needs from food, so items any diet must supply.

clue.text: Story worker's presented for person handling finances

parts.note: an account is a narrative
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A tale about an employee who looks after money.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant keeps and checks financial records.

clue.text: Authentic quality of minister, one attached to Exeter?

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
I is the Roman numeral one
Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, an example of a city, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A clergyman's genuineness, as one belonging to Exeter Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonicity is the status of being accepted as genuine, like a book admitted to the scriptural canon.

clue.text: Female wants listener to show concern

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A woman wants someone to hear her out and be worried.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear for something is to be anxious or worried about it.

clue.text: Are coins unearthed from plot?

indicators.note: unearthed means dug up, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A metal detectorist wonders whether a field holds buried coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unearthed' shuffles ARE COINS; 'plot' looks like a piece of land but is a story outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the storyline of a film or play.

clue.text: Result of gym being closed? Negative response

definitions.meaning: with the gym shut there is ..., physical education, read as two words
an informal way of saying no

explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual no, while the first reading splits it into no plus the school abbreviation for gym class.

clue.text: Hard to penetrate top man, unusually shady figure

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so the hard abbreviation goes into the other letters
unusually signals the letters of the next two words are set out in an odd order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A shadowy character is difficult for the boss to see through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' shuffles TOP MAN and 'to penetrate' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or apparition is a shadowy figure, an insubstantial presence.

clue.text: Somehow catch a lone fish

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unspecified fashion, a rearrangement of the next three words

explanation.surface: An angler manages to land a solitary fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening word is the anagram signal, rearranging CATCH A LONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The coelacanth is an ancient lobe-finned species once thought extinct, until one was caught in 1938.

clue.text: Refinement in pest is lacking

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following little word is taken out

parts.note: a nuisance is an annoying person, a pest

explanation.surface: A finer point about an absent pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle distinction, a fine shade of meaning.

clue.text: Taken to be part of Bristol enterprise

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something was apparently lifted as part of a Bristol business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Taken to be' is trimmed to 'Taken': 'to be' is a link meaning 'to form', and only 'Taken' swaps for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods have been seized without permission, pilfered.

clue.text: Soldiers being insincere, showing uncooperative attitude?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
someone acting is pretending, being insincere

explanation.surface: Troops faking their feelings show a bad attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting against something means resisting it, hence the question mark for an uncooperative response.

clue.text: Where blood flows, it's said, without effectiveness

indicators.note: it's said marks a phrase heard rather than written, a sound-alike

parts.note: blood runs in a vein, read as two words

explanation.surface: A medical note on circulation that turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' swaps IN VEIN for its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no avail, with no useful result, is doing it uselessly.

clue.text: Huge game of two halves, first to last

indicators.text: of two halves, first to last
indicators.note: the word is split into two halves and the first half goes to the end

explanation.surface: An enormous match, the proverbial game of two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: GA and ME swap places. 'A game of two halves' is a football commentator's cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for enormous or tremendous.

clue.text: The thing badly placed in gallery to amuse

indicators.note: placed in puts the following pieces inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries
it means the thing
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A poorly hung artwork in a gallery delights visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous set of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or tickle pleasantly, so to entertain or delight.

clue.text: Support that often comes with ruin

definitions.meaning: a frame or stand holding things up, such as a wine or plate holder
the phrase ... and ruin means decay and collapse

explanation.definitionFit: A rack is a holding frame, and the idiom 'go to rack and ruin' pairs the word with ruin.

clue.text: See doomster rant terribly — that could be me

definitions.text: See doomster rant terribly — that could be me

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A prophet of doom harangues a crowd, and the speaker wonders if they are one too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles DOOMSTER RANT; the whole clue then describes a placard-waving protester who might be the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester ranting about doom at a rally is a street protester, someone marching for a cause.
